posts.title: Delicious Vegan Dumpling Bake Recipe You Need to Try!
posts.excerpt: The health scare that changed how I cook, and what I'd tell anyone standing where I was standing.
posts.body:
If you love dumplings but want a fresh, plant-based twist, this vegan dumpling bake recipe is perfect for you. It combines the comforting texture of baked dumplings with a rich, creamy sauce made from coconut milk and fresh vegetables. This dish is a great example of easy vegan recipes that bring bold flavors and satisfying textures to your table. Whether you are a seasoned vegan foodie or just exploring vegan cooking, this recipe will quickly become a favorite.Before you start, gather these ingredients to make your vegan dumpling bake:

#### 
**Ingredients You Will Need**

Before you start, gather these ingredients to make your vegan dumpling bake:

* **Dumplings or wantons**: Use store-bought vegan dumplings or homemade ones if you prefer.
* **Jasmine rice or quinoa**  ( quinoa is higher in protien)
* **Coconut milk or coconut cream**: Full-fat coconut milk adds creaminess and a subtle sweetness.
* **Vegetables**: Bell peppers, mushrooms, spinach, and carrots (all optional)
* **Garlic and ginger**: Freshly minced for flavor.
* **Thai curry paste** (teaspoon)
* **Miso** tablespoon
* **Soy sauce, tamari or coconut amino**: For a salty, umami kick.
* **Bok Choy**: For garnish and freshness.
* **Chili oil**: For flavor
* **Coconut cream (my perference) cornstarch or arrowroot powder**: To thicken the sauce.
* **Salt, pepper, garlic powerder, onion powder, paprika**: To taste.
* **Seseme oil**
* **Chili crips** 

This combination creates a creamy, flavorful sauce that complements the dumplings perfectly.

## How to Prepare the Vegan Dumpling Bake

Follow these steps for a smooth cooking experience:

1. **Preheat your oven** to 375°F (190°C).
2. **Baking dish**: Standard medium baking dish or depending on the amount of dumplings
3. **Prepare the sauce**: Add garlic and ginger, sauté until fragrant. Add all the seasons and aromatics: Thai chili sauce, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika 
4. **Add coconut milk and coconut amino** (soy sauce for non-vegans) to the pan. Stir well.
5. **Thicken the sauce** by coconut cream (some may like using cornstarch to thicken their sauce), Stir until the sauce thickens.
6. **Arrange the bok choy then the dumplings** on top in a baking dish in a single layer.
7. **Pour the sauce** evenly over the dumplings or underneath (your choice) 
8. **Bake uncovered** for 20-25 minutes until the dumplings are golden and the sauce bubbles. (If you choose to cover the dish the dumplings will be softer)
9. **Place the bok choy on top of jasmine rice then layer your dumplings  ( or garnish with green onions for a simple touch)**  before serving.

This process is straightforward and ideal for anyone looking to try easy vegan recipes that don’t require complicated steps.

## Tips for Perfect Vegan Dumplings

* **Choose dumplings carefully**: Some store-bought dumplings contain egg or dairy. Look for clearly labeled vegan options or make your own using vegan wrappers and fillings.
* **Make your own wantons**: If you want a hands-on approach, prepare vegan wantons filled with tofu, mushrooms, lentil mixture and herbs.
* **Use fresh coconut milk**: Canned coconut milk works well, but fresh coconut milk can enhance the flavor.
* **Add spices**: Try adding chili flakes or five-spice powder for an extra kick.
* **Serve with sides**: Pair your bake with steamed greens or a fresh salad for a balanced meal.

  ![So Yummy! Vegan dumplings and vegetables baked in coconut milk sauce in a ceramic dish](assets/uploads/screenshot-2026-08-08-at-15.24.39.png)

posts.title: Vegan Miso Butter Cabbage
posts.excerpt: Not every substitute is worth it. These five are the ones I make on repeat.
posts.body:
Cabbage is often overlooked in the kitchen, but it holds incredible potential for creating **savory vegan food** that satisfies both comfort and health needs. This Vegan Miso Butter Cabbage recipe transforms humble cabbage into a rich, flavorful dish that appeals to vegan foodies and anyone interested in clean eating or plant-based meals. It’s a simple, quick recipe that brings out the best in cabbage with the umami depth of miso and the creamy texture of vegan butter.

![](assets/uploads/screenshot-2026-08-08-at-15.32.14.png)

## Why Choose Vegan Miso Butter Cabbage



This dish fits perfectly into a **healthy vegan** lifestyle without sacrificing flavor. Cabbage is low in calories but rich in fiber, vitamins C and K, and antioxidants. Adding miso, a fermented soybean paste, introduces probiotics and a deep umami flavor that enhances the dish’s complexity. The vegan butter adds a creamy, comforting texture that makes this recipe a great example of **comfort food** that is also nourishing.



For vegan foodies, this recipe offers a chance to explore bold flavors while keeping the meal clean and plant based. It’s versatile enough to serve as a side dish or a main when paired with grains or tofu.



## Ingredients You Will Need



* 1 medium head of green or red cabbage, sliced into triangles 
* 2 tablespoons vegan butter  
* 2 tablespoons white or yellow miso paste  
* 1 tablespoon soy sauce, coconut amino or tamari (for a gluten-free sauce)  
* 1 cup of raw cashews  
* 1/4 of a cup of Nutritional yeast for the cheese flavor
* 1/2 cup of hemp seeds for high **protein** 
* 1 cup of coconut cream or coconut milk (depends on on thick you want to sauce)
* 2 cloves garlic, minced  
* 1 shallot
* 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger (optional) 
* 1 tablespoon chili flake oil or roasted sesame seeds (optional) as a garnish
* Salt and pepper to taste 
* Paprka, garlic powder, onion powder 
* 1 tablespoon water or vegetable broth (to loosen sauce if needed)



## How to Make Vegan Miso Butter Cabbage



### Step 1: Prepare the Cabbage

Start by removing the outer leaves of the cabbage if they are damaged. Cut the cabbage into quarters, remove the core, then slice it thinly. 

### Step 2: Cook the Cabbage

Heat a large skillet or cast iron skillet, wok or large ceremic sauce pan over medium heat. Add a small splash of oil or a bit of vegan butter to prevent sticking. Add the sliced cabbage to be braised for about 4 minutes (2 mins on both sides) until it starts to soften but still retains some crunch from braising. 

### Step 3: Make the Miso Butter Sauce

In the same pan with medium high heat, combine the vegan butter, dry seasonings ( pre-mixed) miso paste, tamari or coconut amino (tamari and coconut amino are optional)  minced garlic, and grated ginger ( ginger is ptional) until everything is translucent  Add the nutritional yeast for a cheesy flavor at the end.  Mix well until you get a smooth sauce. This mixture will be the heart of the dish, delivering a rich, savory flavor.  The optionsl ingridents will add and extra layer of flavor but can be left out and this dish will still be flavorable!

### Step 4: Add the Miso Butter Sauce

Lower the heat and add the miso butter mixture to the pan. Add the cabbage gently to coat every piece with the sauce. If the mixture feels too thick, add a tablespoon of water or vegetable broth to loosen it. Cook for another 3-4 minutes, allowing the cabbage to absorb the flavors fully.

### Step 5: Finish and Serve

Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if needed. Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds on top for a nutty crunch and extra texture or chili oil flakes. Serve immediately as a side or over steamed rice or quinoa for a complete meal or as the main dish with green leafy, steamed okra and roasted potatoes. 

![](assets/uploads/screenshot-2026-08-08-at-15.31.16.png)

## Tips for Perfect Vegan Miso Butter Cabbage

* Use fresh, firm cabbage for the best texture. Avoid cabbage with brown spots or wilted leaves.  
* Miso paste varies in saltiness and intensity. Start with less and add more to taste.  
* For extra depth, add sliced shiitake mushrooms or chopped scallions during cooking.  
* Toast sesame seeds lightly in a dry pan before adding to enhance their flavor.  
* This dish reheats well and can be stored in the fridge for up to 3 days.

## Why This Recipe Appeals to Vegan Foodies and Healthy Food Enthusiasts

This recipe balances **comfort food** with clean eating principles. It uses whole, plant-based ingredients and avoids processed additives. The miso adds a fermented element that supports gut health, while the vegan butter provides richness without dairy. It’s a great example of how **savory vegan food** can be indulgent and nourishing at the same time.

For vegan foodies, this dish offers a new way to enjoy cabbage beyond salads or boiled sides. It’s a flavorful, satisfying option that fits well into meal prep or weeknight dinners.

## Bringing It All Together

Vegan Miso Butter Cabbage is a simple, delicious recipe that elevates cabbage into a **plant based** dish full of flavor and texture. It suits anyone looking for **healthy vegan** meals that don’t compromise on taste or comfort. Whether you are a seasoned vegan foodie or just exploring **clean eating**, this recipe offers a fresh way to enjoy a classic vegetable.

~ Bella Veganista

posts.title: Savory Vegan Gnocchi in Creamy Coconut Sauce with Blackened Lion's Mane Mushrooms
posts.excerpt: Gnocchi is a beloved comfort food, but traditional recipes often rely on dairy and eggs. This vegan version uses coconut cream to create a rich, creamy sauce that perfectly complements pillowy gnocchi.
posts.body:
Gnocchi is a beloved comfort food, but traditional recipes often rely on dairy and eggs. This vegan version uses coconut cream to create a rich, creamy sauce that perfectly complements pillowy gnocchi. Topping it with blackened Lion's Mane mushrooms adds a smoky, meaty texture that elevates the dish. This recipe offers a satisfying plant-based meal that’s both indulgent and nourishing.

![](assets/uploads/screenshot-2026-08-08-at-15.41.24.png)

## Why Choose Coconut Cream for Vegan Gnocchi?



Coconut cream brings a natural richness and smooth texture that mimics dairy cream without overpowering the dish. It blends beautifully with herbs and spices, creating a luscious sauce that clings to each gnocchi piece. Unlike nut-based creams, coconut cream is allergy-friendly and widely available.



* Adds a subtle sweetness that balances savory flavors  
* Thickens sauces naturally without starches  
* Provides healthy fats that enhance satiety



Using coconut cream keeps this recipe simple and accessible while delivering a decadent mouthfeel.



## Preparing the Gnocchi



Making gnocchi from scratch is easier than many think and yields a tender, fluffy texture. Here’s a quick overview:



1. **Choose starchy potatoes** like Russets for the best consistency.  
2. **Boil and mash** potatoes until smooth, avoiding lumps.  
3. **Mix in flour and a pinch of salt** to form a soft dough.  
4. **Roll the dough into ropes** and cut into bite-sized pieces.  
5. **Boil gnocchi** until they float, signaling they are cooked through.
6. **Or buy gnoochi** in your local market as a shortcut. 



For a vegan twist, avoid eggs and rely on potato starch and flour to bind the dough. This keeps the gnocchi light and tender.



## Blackening Lion's Mane Mushrooms



Lion's Mane mushrooms have a unique texture that resembles seafood or shredded meat when cooked. Blackening them adds a smoky, charred flavor that contrasts beautifully with the creamy sauce.



* Lions mane mushroom will be cook whole no need to break into thick pieces  
* Toss with smoked paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper  
* Heat a cast iron skillet until very hot, then sear mushrooms on each side until blackened and crispy edges form



This method intensifies the mushroom’s natural umami and adds depth to the dish.

![](assets/uploads/screenshot-2026-08-08-at-15.41.29.png)

## Making the Creamy Coconut Sauce



The sauce is simple but packed with flavor. Here’s how to bring it together:



* Sauté minced garlic and shallots or red onions in olive oil until fragrant  
* Add salt, pepper, paprika, onion poweder and garlic poweder.  **Optional:** and fresh herbs like thyme or sage to give it a different flavor
* add coconut cream and stir to combine for flavor and thickness
* Simmer gently until the sauce thickens slightly  
* Add vegetable bouillon to loosen the coconut sauce as needed
* Add 1/2 cup of white cooking wine (or to taste)
* Add vegan Gouda Cheese. Stir.
* Simmer a little more allowing the flavors to merge



The sauce should be silky and coat the gnocchi without being too heavy.



## Assembling the Dish



Once the gnocchi are cooked and drained (if making gnoochi from scratch). Or add the gnoochi from the package and toss them gently in the warm coconut sauce. Plate the gnocchi and top generously with the blackened Lion's Mane mushrooms. Garnish with fresh parsley or microgreens for a pop of color and freshness. Or garnish with grilled jalapeno and grilled mexican corn to change up the flavor for a cultural experience.



This dish pairs well with sauteed swiss chard, a crisp green salad or roasted seasonal vegetables for a complete meal.

![](assets/uploads/screenshot-2026-08-08-at-15.41.35.png)

## Tips for Success



* Use dry potatoes for the gnocchi dough to avoid sogginess.  (if making gnoochi from scratch)
* Don’t overcrowd the pan when blackening mushrooms to ensure proper searing.  
* Adjust the thickness of the sauce by simmering longer or adding a splash of vegetable broth.  
* Experiment with herbs like rosemary or basil to customize the flavor profile.
